clue.text: Is he brown all over first?

definitions.text: Is he brown all over first?

parts.words: Is he brown all over first?
parts.note: a sunbather who strips completely tans evenly all over, with no white strap marks, so is the first to be uniformly brown

explanation.surface: A question about who in a group will be the first to get an all-over tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes without clothes in the sun tans everywhere, so the question describes a naturist.

clue.text: Scent for following, so crawling along?

parts.note: nose can mean a sense of smell or a scent
to tail means in order to follow

explanation.surface: A hound sniffing to track its quarry, inching forward along the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic queued nose to tail is bumper to bumper and so moves at a crawl.

clue.text: Order to pay soldiers being transferred

definitions.meaning: a bank ... is a written order for payment of money
a detachment of troops sent from one unit to another

explanation.surface: Instructions to pay troops who are being moved elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Draft means both a banker's payment order and a body of soldiers detached for service.

clue.text: Separate federal agents in group

indicators.note: the agents are placed inside the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are American FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Splitting up FBI agents within a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment something is to divide it into parts, so to separate it.

clue.text: Steal Jack's land

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman), here with its possessive S
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A sailor's property is being taken from him.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is a formal or euphemistic way of saying to remove or steal it.

clue.text: Deprived female's lost hat

indicators.note: the letter for female has gone missing from the word

parts.note: bereft means deprived
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A deprived woman who has lost her hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a flat round soft cap, so a type of hat.

clue.text: Building not hot enough at first for Australian shrub

indicators.note: the letter for hot is taken away

parts.note: a theatre is a building
H stands for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: only the opening letter of enough is used

explanation.surface: A building that is not warm enough for a delicate plant from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hot' removes H from THEATRE to leave TEATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea tree is an Australian shrub, source of tea tree oil.

clue.text: Island's holy day

definitions.meaning: ... Day, the feast of Christ's rising into heaven, forty days after Easter

explanation.surface: An island's special religious holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascension names both a South Atlantic island and the Christian feast day.

clue.text: Carry toddler to back of queue

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the last letter of queue is used

explanation.surface: Carrying a small child to the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry something, especially a load or gun.

clue.text: Entertainer is a good man, an exceptionally good man

parts.note: ST, saint, is a crossword convention for a good man
a ripper is slang for an excellent person or thing

explanation.surface: Praise for a performer as a fine and outstanding fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is a performer who undresses for an audience, so a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Murder — tough hasn't finished concealing corpse,

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps around and hides the next piece
the synonym is cut short, its final letter dropped

parts.note: stern means hard or tough
in theatre slang, to corpse is to laugh involuntarily on stage

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a killer struggling to hide the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corpse' looks like a dead body, but it is actors' slang for breaking into giggles on stage; 'hasn't finished' drops the last letter and 'concealing' wraps the result around.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is a synonym for killing on a brutal scale, so it can stand for murder.

clue.text: A national course

parts.note: a Scot is a national of Scotland

explanation.surface: A course of study that covers the whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is an English racecourse, home of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, so it is an example of a course.

clue.text: Rodent, teeth grinding, clung on to piece without giving up

indicators.note: the scrambled letters grip the next piece, holding it inside them
teeth grinding are being worked about, so their letters are rearranged along with those of rodent

parts.note: a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A rat gnaws stubbornly at a morsel, refusing to let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grinding' shuffles RODENT and TEETH into TOTHE TEREND, and 'clung on to' places BIT in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying on to the bitter end is an idiom for persisting to the last and never surrendering.

clue.text: Plant commander has to criticise like this

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
to pan is to criticise harshly
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: An officer is told to criticise in a particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapanthus is a flowering plant, the African lily, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Understood that all children instinctively think using their heads

indicators.note: only the heads, the initial letters, of these five words are used

explanation.surface: A comment on how all children know things by instinct, using their own brains.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'think using their heads'; the extra 're' is an OCR addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit describes something implied or understood without being spoken aloud in words.

clue.text: Dress down, with sack in luggage

parts.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, to dress them down
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: Advice to dress casually and pack a sack in the cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbag is a travelling bag made of carpet fabric, an item of luggage.

clue.text: Yorkshire town opting to welcome head of state

indicators.note: the word for opting takes in the next piece like a guest

parts.note: picking means choosing or opting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the British head of state

explanation.surface: A northern town choosing to receive a visiting dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickering is a market town in North Yorkshire, so it is an example of a Yorkshire town.

clue.text: The cops struggling to get to Welsh town

indicators.note: the police are in difficulty, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Police officers battling to reach a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges THE COPS into CHEPSTO; Chepstow is a town in Monmouthshire, Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a Welsh border town known for its castle and racecourse.

clue.text: Concerning answer, it's available for use if needed

parts.note: in re is Latin for in the matter of, concerning
to answer can mean to serve or suffice, as in 'that will answer the purpose'

explanation.surface: A reply about something that can be kept on hand for emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held back for later use if required is said to be kept in reserve, a common idiom.

clue.text: The Spanish indulged in cabbage and sausage

indicators.note: the Spanish article goes inside the cabbage

parts.note: a savoy is a type of cabbage
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards enjoying a meal of cabbage and sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a spicy smoked sausage, a British fish-and-chip shop staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a seasoned red pork sausage, so an example of a sausage.

clue.text: Conceited type embracing popular young beauty

indicators.note: the conceited fellow wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a pup is a conceited, cheeky young man
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A vain man with his arms around a fashionable young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is an attractive person, usually young, whose picture is pinned on walls by admirers.

clue.text: How one of Santa's team moved with springing steps?

definitions.text: How one of Santa's team moved with springing steps?

parts.words: How one of Santa's team moved with springing steps?
parts.note: one of the reindeer pulling Santa's sleigh is named for bounding gait, and the verb of that name describes leaping movement

explanation.surface: A question about how a reindeer pranced across the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To move with high springing steps is to bound like a lively horse, matching the reindeer named Prancer.

clue.text: Forces army into changing to fuel supplier

parts.note: the armed forces are the services
TA is the Territorial Army

indicators.note: the letters of into are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Military forces drafting the army into a change of plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' reads like a verb, but it is the noun for the armed services; 'changing' rearranges the word 'into' to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A service station is a roadside garage selling petrol, so it supplies fuel to motorists.

clue.text: Conspirator's fall when last two notes seized

indicators.note: the notes are taken away from the word

parts.note: a cascade is a waterfall
D and E are musical notes, here the final two letters

explanation.surface: A plotter's downfall comes when two musical notes are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, in history and in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the plotters against Julius Caesar, so he is a conspirator.

clue.text: State "I had a house"

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone saying they once owned a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Staff in union

definitions.meaning: an association of people joined by a shared interest

explanation.surface: Employees belonging to a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Club means both a heavy staff used as a weapon and a society or union of members.

clue.text: Telling stories about people, will I be lying? To some extent

indicators.note: To some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone worried whether spreading gossip about others counts as lying.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is publishing false, damaging statements about someone, a legal sense of telling stories about people.

clue.text: Welsh cocoa's no source of energy; it could make someone sluggish

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder could be made into the answer once rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
E is the physics symbol for energy, and 'no source of energy' says it is missing from the pool

explanation.surface: A Welsh hot drink that gives no energy and leaves you lethargic.
explanation.walkthrough: WELSH COCOA minus the E for energy ('no source of energy') leaves letters that 'it could make' into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a person who moves or works slowly, an informal term for a dawdler.

clue.text: Unpleasant character, Moneybags, endlessly splashing out

indicators.note: the remaining letters are thrown about and rearranged
the word moneybags loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A nasty rich man who keeps spending lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MONEYBAGS to MONEYBAG, and 'splashing out' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is a frightening figure or a hated person, so an unpleasant character.

clue.text: Two-thirds tuneful, but wholly repulsive

indicators.note: only the last six of the nine letters, two thirds of the word, are kept

parts.note: melodious means tuneful

explanation.surface: A piece of music that is mostly melodic yet completely revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds' drops the first three letters MEL of MELODIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or deeply offensive, a direct synonym for repulsive.
